findings.note: The fixed offset repeats canon.rs:1762's widths, and an overflowing leading cell would shift columns. Overflow only happens when a leading column renders 'FLAG …' (mark(), canon.rs:1856), and the same test's 'discrepancy flags: 0 slot(s)' assertion already catches that, so the consequence is negligible.

Says a modality/subject/unstructured flag on REQ-0007 would now pass silently, but the same test asserts 'discrepancy flags: 0 slot(s)', and ClaimVerdict::flags (canon.rs:1296-1311) counts those columns, so the regression is still caught.
the_annotation_cell_is_read_at_its_column test only asserts !cell.starts_with("ann"), so a wrong CELL_START (e.g. 0, whole row starting 'REQ-X') still passes; it never asserts the cell's content.
Same latent fixed-offset/overflow fragility as F01. In the corpus only a FLAG makes a leading cell overflow, and the flags: 0 summary assertion catches that.

is_qualitative_convention now accepts an empty operator (canon.rs:1387), while ADR 0014:193 and docs/claim-format.md:117 still define the triple as operator EQ, so the docs contradict the widened code.
The same claim as F02. Narrowing the REQ-0007 FLAG check loses no coverage, because the 'discrepancy flags: 0 slot(s)' assertion in the same test fails on any flag in any column.

The helper test builds its row from the same hardcoded widths as CELL_START, so it exercises nothing canon.rs prints; row.contains("ann") holds by construction. It cannot catch layout drift. It overlaps G2 in weakness but is a different defect (no link to the product).
